topics.topic: Authoritative dependency vulnerability audit and package set for deployment
questions: Is a deploy required to pass the requirements-resolution audit, the installed-image audit, or both, and which result governs when they differ?
Are both checks required, or which command and package set is authoritative for deciding whether the deploy passes?
Must deployment pass the requirements-resolution audit, the installed-image audit, or both, and which result is authoritative if the resolved package sets differ?

quotes:
The check is reproducible: `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt`, which
resolves the pins with the packages pip installs for them and queries the
PyPI advisory database (OSV) at the time of the deploy.

The check runs inside the built image against what is
installed there (`pip-audit --local`), so the audited set is the shipped
set.
judgement.divergence: The requirements-resolution audit can pass while the installed-image audit blocks, or vice versa; the deployment operator observes whether the release proceeds.
judgement.why: A32 names two different package sets and commands as the deployment check without saying that both must pass or which governs.

witness.initial: The built image contains transitive package T version 1 with an advisory, while a fresh resolution of the four direct pins selects T version 2 without that advisory.
events: The deployment operator runs the required pre-deploy vulnerability check after building the image.
outcomes: The `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt` check audits T version 2, passes, and permits deployment.
The `pip-audit --local` check audits installed T version 1 and blocks deployment.
basis:
Before a deploy, the pinned versions are checked against a public
known-vulnerability database; a pin with a known vulnerability that affects
the portal is not deployed until it is updated through the Factory route.

The check is reproducible: `pip-audit -r deploy/requirements.txt`, which
resolves the pins with the packages pip installs for them and queries the
PyPI advisory database (OSV) at the time of the deploy.

The check runs inside the built image against what is
installed there (`pip-audit --local`), so the audited set is the shipped
set.

precedent.topic: Expense-intake authorization, content-validation, and assignment-check order
quotes:
1. The route authorizes with
   `capability:authorization_guard.authorize_staff_project_mutation`.
2. `capability:expense_intake.create_expense_from_recognition` accepts only a
   confirmed complete result of a supported contract version, validates the
   total and the explicit allocations — every section of the project
   (`capability:budget_management.validate_project_section`), positive amounts,
   exact sum, no proportional split — then in one transaction looks up the
   `recognized_document_id`: absent — insert the expense, its allocations and
   one client-visible document and append `expense.create`; same fingerprint —
   return the existing expense as replay; different — conflict.
precedent.why: The later flow orders staff project authorization before recognition, item, money, allocation, and replay validation.

topics.topic: Whether archived-but-active Registry projects permit access-management creation
questions: When validation returns `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, and `is_active=true`, must creation of a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant be allowed or rejected?

When a decoded validation answer has `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, and `is_active=true`, must creation of a viewer grant, staff assignment, or producer grant succeed or be rejected as an archived project?
When validation returns `exists=true`, `is_active=true`, and `status="archived"`, is access-management creation allowed or rejected as an archived project?

quotes:
No new viewer grant, staff assignment
or producer grant is created for an archived project, because each creation
validates that the Registry project is active (accepted notes
`grant_viewer_project`, `assign_staff_project`, `grant_producer_project`).

Only then is a validation answer read by its caller,
as A5 says: `exists = false` is not found; an existing project is archived
for the project guard when its `status` is not `active`, and for the grant
and assignment operations when `is_active = false`. The gateway returns a
decoded validation answer as it is and raises no failure for it; it does not
check that `exists`, `is_active` and `status` agree, and each caller trusts
only the field A5 names for it.
judgement.divergence: An inconsistent Registry answer with archived status and `is_active=true` either refuses access creation or permits and persists it; the administrator and grantee observe the difference.
judgement.why: State 0 rejects new access for an archived project, while State 2 directs access-management callers to ignore `status` and trust a possibly inconsistent `is_active=true`.

witness.initial: An active administrator has `portal.access.manage`; no access record exists for project P; Registry validation returns `exists=true`, `status="archived"`, and `is_active=true`.
events: The administrator requests creation of a viewer grant for P.
The portal validates P through Registry.
outcomes: R0-24 rejects creation because the project is archived, and no grant is stored.
A6 trusts `is_active=true` for the grant operation, so the grant is stored and audited.
basis:
Creating, revoking and re-issuing client viewers, their access links and
project grants, staff accounts and assignments, service principals, their
credentials and producer grants all require the access-management capability,
which only administrators hold (R2).

The gateway returns a
decoded validation answer as it is and raises no failure for it; it does not
check that `exists`, `is_active` and `status` agree, and each caller trusts
only the field A5 names for it.

topics.topic: Global memory bound and overflow behavior for the viewer-entry limiter
questions: Must the limiter impose a global memory/key bound with defined eviction or refusal behavior, or is memory intentionally unbounded across distinct client addresses within a window?
Must the implementation impose a global key/entry bound, or must it admit arbitrarily many distinct client-address keys within one window?

quotes: Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime settings before expensive work; viewer entry attempts are rate limited per client network address and route, with bounded memory and a concealed answer, the address read only from the connection, never from a forwarded header, cookie or secret.

that is the whole bound —
there is no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction.
judgement.divergence: The limiter either retains arbitrarily many distinct address keys or imposes some global refusal or eviction bound; clients and the service operator observe admission and memory differences.
judgement.why: A limiter with no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction is not globally bounded in memory during a window.

bases.passage: Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime settings before expensive work; viewer entry attempts are rate limited per client network address and route, with bounded memory and a concealed answer, the address read only from the connection, never from a forwarded header, cookie or secret.

that is the whole bound —
there is no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction.

unsupported_sides: Request bodies and binary responses are bounded by runtime settings before expensive work; viewer entry attempts are rate limited per client network address and route, with bounded memory and a concealed answer, the address read only from the connection, never from a forwarded header, cookie or secret.

that is the whole bound —
there is no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction.

witness.initial: The limiter is empty and permits ten attempts per address per sixty seconds.
events: One million distinct client addresses each submit one viewer-entry attempt within the same window.
outcomes: The no-cap rule admits all attempts and retains one million keys.
The bounded-memory rule requires refusing attempts or evicting keys after a finite global bound.
witness.observer: The requesting clients and the service operator
basis:
The limiter is a sliding-window log per (client address,
route) key: an entry attempt (`POST /auth/viewer/enter`) is refused with
HTTP 429 and an empty body, before any code verification and without a
session, when that key already has `RuntimeSettings.viewer_entry_rate_limit_attempts`
attempts within the last `viewer_entry_rate_limit_window_seconds`; every
admitted attempt counts, valid or not, refused attempts are not counted, and
on every attempt the entries older than the window are dropped across all
keys and a key left without entries is removed, so the log never holds more
than the attempts admitted within one window; that is the whole bound —
there is no cap on distinct keys and no other eviction.

topics.topic: Portal enforcement of snapshot section non-emptiness and source-section-ID uniqueness
questions: Are non-emptiness and `source_section_id` uniqueness input-model constraints enforced by the portal, or merely unenforced producer obligations?

quotes:
**In the running service:** "non-empty, unique `source_section_id`" is
the producer's obligation, not a portal check: the import refuses
neither an empty section list nor repeated `source_section_id` values.
judgement.why: The text explicitly makes both conditions producer obligations and says the portal does not enforce them.

topics.topic: ProjectOverview shape and validation after a Registry context-read failure
questions: What are the actual `ProjectOverview` fields and validation rule after a post-guard Registry context read fails?

quotes:
`ProjectOverview`: six pairs — project, budget, expenses, progress, payments,
photos — each a `ViewAvailability` and a value present only when available.

A21 (derived at read time, nothing persisted), A27 and Factory
`d2c4511ea119`: a part whose builder answers `ScopedNotFoundError` is
`not_configured`, a persistence or Registry failure `temporarily_unavailable`;
no zero is fabricated; viewer photos are client-visible only.
judgement.why: State 5 defines ProjectOverview as six availability/value pairs and converts a Registry context failure into temporary unavailability.

topics.topic: Strict typing versus coercion when decoding snapshot publication requests
questions: Must external snapshot request decoding be strict about JSON types, or may it coerce compatible values before A7 validation?

quotes:
A body that lacks a field the request model requires, or carries one of
the wrong type (identity fields included), is refused by request decoding
(HTTP 422) before the bearer credential is checked
judgement.why: Whether a JSON value is coerced or rejected is an exact request-schema and decoding contract owned by State 6.

questions: Does every reported advisory block deployment, or only an advisory assessed as affecting the portal?

quotes:
Every advisory it
reports for any resolved package blocks the deploy; "affects the portal"
is not judged case by case, so an advisory for an unused optional feature
blocks too.
judgement.why: The normative rule explicitly requires every reported advisory to block without a portal-relevance assessment.
